landmarks.name: Vallée de Mai Nature Reserve
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site on Praslin Island, known for its unique palm forest and the rare Coco de Mer palm.

wiki.extract: Vallée de Mai Nature Reserve is a nature park and UNESCO World Heritage Site on the island of Praslin, Seychelles. It consists of a well-preserved palm forest, flagship species made up of the island endemic coco de mer, as well as five other endemic palms.

landmarks.name: Anse Source d'Argent
landmarks.writeup: Famous beach on La Digue Island, renowned for its pink sand, granite boulders, and clear turquoise waters.

wiki.extract: Anse Source d'Argent is a beach situated in the southwest coast of La Digue, Seychelles. It is listed in Lonely Planet as one of the world's best beaches in 2024.

landmarks.name: Morne Seychellois National Park
landmarks.writeup: Largest national park on Mahé Island, featuring hiking trails and diverse flora and fauna.

wiki.extract: Morne Seychellois is the highest peak in Seychelles. Morne Seychellois is located on the island of Mahé in the Morne Seychellois National Park.

cultural_events.name: Festival Kreol
cultural_events.writeup: Annual cultural festival celebrating Creole heritage with music, dance, food, and art.

wiki.extract:
Seychelles, officially the Republic of Seychelles, is an archipelagic country consisting of 115 islands in the Indian Ocean. Its capital and largest city, Victoria, is 1,500 kilometres east of mainland Africa. Nearby island countries and territories include the Maldives, Comoros, Madagascar, Mauritius, and the French overseas departments of Mayotte and Réunion to the south; and the Chagos Archipelago to the east.
Seychelles is the smallest country in Africa as well as the least populated sovereign African country, with an estimated population of 100,600 in 2022.

cultural_events.name: Independence Day
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrated on June 29th, marking Seychelles' independence from the United Kingdom in 1976.

wiki.extract: Independence Day is celebrated annually on 15 August as a public holiday in India commemorating the nation's independence from the United Kingdom on 15 August 1947. On this day the Indian Independence Act 1947 came into effect, transferring legislative sovereignty to the Indian Constituent Assembly. India attained independence following the independence movement noted for largely non-violent resistance and civil disobedience led by the Indian National Congress under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi.

food_writeup: Seychellois cuisine is a blend of African, French, Indian, and Chinese influences, featuring seafood, tropical fruits, and spices. Popular dishes include grilled fish, octopus curry, and ladob, a dessert made from plantains or breadfruit.
brief_history: Seychelles was uninhabited until the 18th century when it was colonized by the French, later becoming a British colony. It gained independence in 1976 and has since developed into a stable republic with a focus on tourism and conservation.

current_conflicts: Seychelles is generally peaceful with no significant internal or external conflicts at present.

commentary.inflation_management: Seychelles' inflation reflects its 2008 regime change. Before the float, price controls suppressed inflation (-1.9% in 2006); the October 2008 float and devaluation sent it to 37.0% in 2008 and 31.8% in 2009, the series highs, before collapsing to -2.4% in 2010. Since then the central bank's reserve-money framework with a floating rupee has delivered low inflation: mostly 1-4% through the 2010s, 9.8% in 2021 on the COVID shock, then -1.0% in 2023 and 0.3% in both 2024 and 2025. The float has been the key: it absorbs tourism shocks that would otherwise break a peg, and the central bank has earned credibility.
commentary.debt_management: Seychelles executed one of the world's most successful debt workouts. From 192.1% of GDP in 2008, the series high, the October 2008 default and IMF program brought a comprehensive restructuring: the ratio fell to 48.9% by 2019, the series low, through sustained primary surpluses that were among the world's largest. COVID's tourism collapse pushed it back to 76.7% in 2020, but the rebound has brought it to a projected 52.2% in 2025. The debt is a mix of external (restructured bonds) and domestic; sustainability is comfortable, and Seychelles is the rare African case where a debt crisis was fully resolved through adjustment rather than relief.

key_events.event: October 2008: defaulted on a $230m Eurobond; IMF program began; rupee floated; inflation hit 37.0%.
Sustained fiscal surpluses cut debt from 192.1% to under 60% of GDP; program completed.
COVID-19 shut down tourism; debt jumped to 76.7% of GDP.
Wavel Ramkalawan won the presidency (2020), the first opposition victory since independence.
Tourism recovered strongly; debt projected at 52.2% of GDP.

commentary.outlook_next_decade: The base case is continued stability: low debt, low inflation, and tourism-led growth, with the floating rupee absorbing shocks. Upside comes from fisheries and the blue economy; downside is climate change, an existential threat to a low-lying archipelago. Uncertainty is low on macro policy, which is exemplary, but high on climate, which no policy can offset.
commentary.caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
